```{python}
import json

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Markdown

summary = json.load(open("outputs/summary.json"))
profiles = pd.read_csv("outputs/cluster_profiles.csv").set_index("cluster")
outcomes = pd.read_csv("outputs/outcomes_by_year.csv")
names = profiles["name"].to_dict()
colors = profiles["color"].to_dict()
features = ["irca", "water_coverage", "sewer_coverage", "ipm", "rural_share", "altitude_m",
            "rainfall_mm", "mdm", "log_sgp_water_pc"]
labels = ["IRCA", "Piped water", "Sewer", "Poverty", "Rural share", "Altitude", "Rainfall",
          "MDM", "log SGP / person"]
```

## The question

- Which **kinds** of municipal zone exist, by drinking-water quality, services and context?
- How do **infant mortality**, **Saber 11** scores and **school dropout** differ between them?
- `{python} f"{summary['kept']:,}"` zone-years, `{python} f"{summary['municipalities']:,}"` municipalities, 2016–2023; IRCA is utility-supplied (prestadores)

## The `{python} summary['k']` kinds

```{python}
t = profiles[["name", "rows", "municipalities", "irca_median"]].rename(
    columns={"name": "Kind", "rows": "Zone-years", "municipalities": "Municipalities",
             "irca_median": "Median IRCA"})
t.index.name = "Cluster"
Markdown(t.to_markdown())
```

## What sets them apart

```{python}
#| fig-alt: "Heatmap of four kinds by nine features from blue (below average) to red (above average)."
z = profiles[[f"z_{f}" for f in features]].to_numpy()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 3.6))
im = ax.imshow(z, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-1.5, vmax=1.5, aspect="auto")
ax.set_xticks(range(len(features)), labels, rotation=30, ha="right")
ax.set_yticks(range(len(profiles)), [f"{c} · {names[c]}" for c in profiles.index])
for i in range(z.shape[0]):
    for j in range(z.shape[1]):
        ax.text(j, i, f"{z[i, j]:+.1f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=8)
fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, label="z (SD from the year's average)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Outcomes by kind

```{python}
#| fig-alt: "Three line charts by year of median infant mortality, Saber 11 score and dropout, one line per kind, with gaps in years without data."
titles = {"infant_mortality": "Infant mortality /1,000", "saber11_mean": "Saber 11 score",
          "dropout_rate": "Dropout (%)"}
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(10, 3.4))
for ax, (col, title) in zip(axes, titles.items()):
    o = outcomes[outcomes["outcome"] == col]
    for c, g in o.groupby("cluster"):
        g = g.set_index("year").reindex(range(2016, 2024))
        ax.plot(g.index, g["median"], marker="o", color=colors[c], label=names[c])
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=10, loc="left")
    ax.set_xticks([2016, 2019, 2022])
fig.legend(*axes[0].get_legend_handles_labels(), loc="lower center", ncol=2, frameon=False,
           bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.14), fontsize=8)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## What this does and does not show

- ✅ Where the kinds are, and how outcomes **differ** between them
- ❌ **Not** a causal effect of water quality: poverty, rurality, health access and reporting differ too
- ⚠️ IRCA is utility-supplied (prestadores); many rural systems are never sampled
